messages:
ana: Heads up — canary rollout of driver 536.1 onto Hopper/SM90 nodes started ~30m ago and we're seeing PTX/kernel load failures in eu-west and ap-southeast canaries :warning:

vijay: Can you paste the logs?

ana: (logs) ```stderr
[2024-06-13T12:02:14Z] ptx_module: load failed: invalid ptx version for sm_90 (expected >= 90.0, found 88.0)
[2024-06-13T12:02:14Z] kernel_lookup: sm90_conv_fp16 not found, falling back to noop
[2024-06-13T12:02:16Z] runtime: fallback path triggered — performance degrade
```

ops-bot: Alert: node pool eu-west-hopper-canary marked DEGRADED (3/10 nodes). NCCL collectives reported timeouts across two pods.

sam: Are we seeing NCCL hangs or just kernel not-found errors?

ana: Both — some jobs hit kernel codegen mismatch and abort, others hang in NCCL allreduce across racks. Canary failure rate ~15% for SM90 workloads.

jen: Suggestion: pause the rollout and rollback canaries immediately. Do we have a quick flag to force PTX JIT fallback?

carlos: You can enable runtime PTX JIT fallback per node: ```bash
rdwnctl node update --label enable_ptx_jit=true --pool eu-west-hopper-canary
# or env for container: export RDW_ENABLE_PTX_JIT=1
```

vijay: Enabled on one pod as test — it recovered but perf regressed ~30% and token throughput dropped. Not ideal for production.

ana: Plan: 1) pause full rollout 2) rollback driver on canaries 3) blacklist 536.1 for SM90 tagged nodes 4) open vendor ticket for PTX codegen change 5) add SM90-specific smoke tests to canary pipeline. @jen can you open the rollback/incident ticket?

jen: Opened INF-4821 and added labels + priority P0. Also kicked the autoscaler to reserve 4 spare H100s in us-west2 to absorb traffic while we stabilize — cost hit estimated ~+$4k/day.

infra-sre-bot: Autoscaler: reserved 4 additional h100s in us-west2 (reservation id rsv-20240613-01).

sam: We should also add a quick kernel smoke suite that runs conv/attention microbenchmarks compiled for sm90 after driver changes. Add to canary pipeline before production rollout.

vijay: FYI NCCL/driver notes: NCCL 2.12 and above generally want drivers >=525, but 536 changed PTX target semantics for SM90 which breaks precompiled kernels. Looks like new driver emits PTX that older nvrtc NVPTX runtime on our containers can't handle.

carlos: Short-term mitigation: label all SM90 hosts with gpu_arch:sm90 and pin them to driver 535.* via nodeSelector / kube label so they won't receive the 536.x rollout. Example: ```bash
kubectl label node <node> gpu_arch=sm90
kubectl patch daemonset h100-drivers -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"driver.version":"535.54"}}}}}'```

jen: Rolling back drivers on eu-west and ap-southeast canaries now. ETA ~20m.

ops-bot: Rollback job started: job_id rb-1718240001 (eu-west).

ops-bot: Rollback complete on canaries. Please re-run smoke-suite.

sam: Smoke-suite results: 12/15 kernels passed. 3 failing tests still showing PTX mismatch on long-conv workloads — looks like some cached artifacts still compiled against newer PTX targets.

ana: Action items: halt rollout globally, pin SM90 nodes to 535.*, blacklist 536.1 for SM90 pools, run artifact cache purge on canaries, open vendor engineering ticket (INF-4821) for driver/PTX semantics, add SM90 smoke tests to canary pipeline, and accept temporary capacity reservation cost. I'll draft a short postmortem and status doc.

jen: Thanks all — leaving the canaries on rollback until vendor confirms fix. :thumbsup:

vijay: I'll also add a check to CI that validates PTX version targets for compiled kernels before we push driver rollouts.

carlos: Note: if vendor releases patched 536.x we should run a small recompile job with nvrtc matching the container runtime and validate before re-enabling.

ana: Good call. Closing this Slack thread, continuing updates in INF-4821 and the status doc. :eyes:
